name: Providence Marriott Downtown
notes: Full-service Marriott hotel, ~351 rooms (listings say 351-354)

Listings describe a brand-new 16-unit professionally managed elevator building on Wayland Square; 2BR ~$2,650-2,975. Assessor yearBuilt 2022 (new construction); one forrent listing mentions a 'condo unit 204' - verify not condo-ized

name: Fox Point Landing (planned as Residences at India Point), 180 George M. Cohan Blvd
notes: Conversion of the former Tockwotton Home (1850s 'Home for Aged Women'; nursing home/assisted living to 2013, then Roosevelt International Academy boarding school) by Dustin Dezube/Providence Living (180 GMC LLC). Zoning approved Apr 2022; NEREJ said completion expected fall 2024; now leasing as Fox Point Landing (Providence Group). Exact CO year not found - likely 2024-25. 71 units planned vs assessor 69

name: Center Place
notes: Luxury downtown apartment tower (studio-3BR, concierge, pool); owned by Hines Global Income Trust (HGIT). Assessor 225 units, built 1991

name: Courtyard by Marriott Providence Downtown (32 Exchange Terrace)
notes: Courtyard Providence Downtown, 219 rooms

name: 95 Lofts
notes: Historic loft conversion redeveloped by Waldorf Capital in 2017 with federal/state historic tax credits; 59 units (assessor 57). Has a Tax Stabilization Agreement; no affordability restriction mentioned. Sold Jan 2026 to Audubon Capital with sister Chestnut Commons (92 units, 180 Friendship St, built 2020)

name: Graduate by Hilton Providence (former Providence Biltmore)
notes: 1922 Biltmore hotel, renamed Graduate Providence 2019; 292-294 rooms

name: Beneficent House
notes: 10-story, 180-unit building (1965) owned by nonprofit Beneficent House (501(c)(4), ruling 1966) whose mission is low-to-moderate income housing; IRS NTEE code = senior citizens' housing; directories call it a senior community with market-rate and subsidized apartments, waitlist, rents ~$720-1,670. Could not confirm a HUD/Section 8 contract or deed restriction - may be senior_living/partly market

name: The Dean Hotel
notes: Boutique hotel, 52 rooms; building built 1912 as an Episcopal church shelter

name: Residence Inn by Marriott Providence Downtown
notes: Extended-stay all-suite hotel opened 2019 (Procaccianti/TPG), 176 suites

name: Rooms & Works Phase II (50 Sprague Street Apartments)
notes: Part of the former Mechanical Fabric Co. mill complex converted to live-work apartments by Rooms & Works (Federico Manaigo / Cromwell Ventures). A listing calls 40-50 Sprague 'Phase II' with 30 residences total; Wikipedia photo caption shows Rooms & Works residences here in 2021. Exact CO year not found (~2019-2021). Historic tax credits; no affordability restriction found

name: Rooms & Works Phase II (40 Sprague Street Apartments)
notes: Zillow: 12-unit building (1-2BR), Rooms & Works Phase II mill conversion of the Mechanical Fabric Co. complex. Wikipedia photo shows 40 Sprague 'in disrepair' in 2017, so residential conversion is post-2017 (CO year not found, likely ~2019-2021). Assessor 34 units may include commercial/live-work spaces

name: Rooms & Works (Mechanical Fabric Company mill)
notes: Historic mill converted to 40 rental apartments + ~11,000 sf commercial (culinary incubator/kitchen); Citizens construction loan Dec 2015, work began 2013; opened ~2016-2019 (exact CO year not found). Market-rate rents ~$1,750-2,400

name: 1290W
notes: New-construction 32-unit elevator building (studio-2BR), listings call it 'brand new'; managed by Westminster Management. Opening year not found online (assessor yearBuilt 2019). No affordability restriction found

name: Strive Lofts
notes: Former Asa Peck Co. storage/jewelry-manufacturing mill (1903-08, later International Graphics) converted by Strive Realty into 56 apartments + ground-floor commercial; conversion began late 2019, ArtInRuins dates redevelopment 2021-2022 with units leasing by Dec 2022 (opened year approximate). Market rents ~$1,700-2,370

name: 530 Broadway Apartments
notes: Listings: 32 units (micro/studio/1BR), 3 stories, 'built in 2020', also described as 'newly renovated'/'brand new'; posted by 530A Broadway LLC. Assessor yearBuilt 1940, so likely a gut rehab or conversion of an older building around 2020 - prior use not found

Nothing found online for this address or owner 'Meadow View Group' (24 units, 1982). Nearby Marvin Gardens II (1688 Westminster) is subsidized; a 'Meadowview Apartments' result from Community Housing Partners appears unrelated. Needs HUD/RIHousing lookup

name: Laurelmead Cooperative
notes: Resident-owned 55+ independent-living cooperative (shareholder units sold, e.g. $320k 2BR); 154 apartments. Cooperative + senior: exempt either way.

name: Wingate Residences on Blackstone Boulevard
notes: Licensed assisted living + memory care (formerly EPOCH Assisted Living on Blackstone Blvd); listings cite 82 AL units + 20 memory care / 96 licensed beds. Assessor 128 units.

name: Wayland Manor
notes: 7-story 1926 rental building, 109 units per apartments.com search snippet, studios-2BR ~$1,400-2,800, 24-hr concierge; no income restriction seen in listings (pages 403 on fetch; data from search snippets).

name: Elmwood Health Center (Elmwood Nursing & Rehabilitation Center)
notes: Nursing home / rehab (directory listings); assessor 70 units likely beds. Institution, not apartments.

name: Former Hood Memorial AME Church apartments
notes: Church-to-apartments conversion (Bluedog Capital Partners): 15 micro/studio/1BR units, city approval Sept 2020; units now listed ~$1,650-2,100. Opening year not found, but must be after late 2020, so likely inside the 5-year new-construction window. No affordability mentioned.

name: Berkshire Place (455 Douglas Ave)
notes: Owner is 455 Douglas Ave Property LLC; Berkshire Place, an assisted living facility, is listed at 455 Douglas Ave. Assessor 210 units are probably beds. Unit count unconfirmed.

name: The Highlands on the East Side
notes: Assisted living + memory care near Miriam Hospital; assessor 74 units.

name: Extended Stay America Suites - Providence
notes: Extended-stay hotel (Expedia lists it also as WoodSpring Suites Providence), nightly from ~$95. Studios also marketed monthly (~$2,249-2,399) as Furnished Studio-Providence. Assessor 123 units = rooms. Built 2016.

name: Capitol Ridge at Providence (Benchmark Senior Living; marketed as 700 Smith St)
notes: Owner KRE-BSL Husky = KKR/Benchmark Senior Living JV; Benchmark operates Capitol Ridge (assisted living + memory care, 168 licensed beds) at 700 Smith St. Matched to this parcel by owner, not by address. Assessor 160 units.

name: Wanskuck Mills
notes: Historic mill conversion by Branch Holdings (bought Dec 2017), historic tax credits. 225 apts + 24,300 sf commercial; phase 1 (60 units) due Sept 2019, more online spring 2021. Unit counts vary by source: 210 (RI tax credit list), 225, 228 (assessor). No affordability found. Phase 2 may fall at the edge of the 5-year window.

name: Edward Cooney House
notes: HUD Section 202 elderly/disabled housing, 27 HUD units (matches assessor 27); owner Wanskuck Housing Corp is a 501(c)(3) for elderly/handicapped housing. Not a cooperative despite the input rule; exempt as project-based subsidized. Also listed as Charlesgate East in one directory.

name: Olmsted Gardens (3 Olmsted Way)
notes: Senior (62+) / disabled 1BR housing managed by The Community Builders; rent 30% of adjusted income for income-restricted units (likely HUD 202/PRAC; program not confirmed). Owner Olmsted Gardens Inc; assessor 52 units, built 2001. Listings use 3 Olmsted Way, matched to this parcel by owner name.

name: The 91 Lofts
notes: Mill converted to loft apartments; Nov 2023 listing says "the latest lofts in a meticulously restored mill building," and other listings say "brand new lofts," which suggests some units opened recently. Studios/lofts ~$800-1,600. Conversion year and total units not confirmed (assessor 102 units).

name: Rear lot of The 91 Lofts mill (91R Hartford Ave)
notes: Assessor class is vacant land (19 units, new-construction-permit flag), owner Ortega Properties LLC. No online info found specifically for 91R; it is the rear parcel behind The 91 Lofts (91 Hartford Ave). Possibly a planned new building; unverified.

name: St. Anthony Mission Church and former rectory
notes: Church parcel (St. Anthony Mission Church, Assumption BVM parish), with a vacant 7,800 sf brick former rectory listed for sale at $325k, pitched for adult daycare/assisted living. Owner is now 549 Plainfield Street LLC, so it may have been sold for redevelopment. No apartment conversion found; assessor 15 units unexplained.

name: Halstead Providence (formerly The Promenade at the Foundry), Sharpe Building
notes: Brown & Sharpe mill complex conversion bought by DSF for $105M in Oct 2021, then renamed Halstead Providence. Sharpe Building has 196 apts (rehab 2015), matching assessor 196 for this parcel; the Promenade Building (237 apts, 2005) is a separate parcel. Luxury market-rate; no affordability mentioned.

name: Hotel Providence (Trademark Collection by Wyndham)
notes: Boutique hotel, 80 rooms incl. 16 suites (matches assessor 80).

name: Renaissance Providence Downtown Hotel (former Masonic Temple, marketed as 5 Avenue of the Arts)
notes: 272-room hotel, matching assessor 272 units; assessor year 2006 = Masonic Temple renovation. Owner RP Providence LLC. Matched by room count and street; the hotel uses No. 5.

name: FOUND Study College Hill (formerly Edge College Hill)
notes: 15-story private student high-rise built 2018 with 202 micro-lofts; per-bedroom leases, roommate matching, furnished. Hawkins Way Capital bought it in 2022 and cites 247 units total across the complex (formal address 100 N Main). Not university-owned. Opening falls just outside the 5-year window.

name: FOUND Study College Hill (100 N Main St portion)
notes: Same owner (100 N Main Owner LLC) as 169 Canal St; the complex formal address is 100 N Main St, and the 2022 sale cites 247 units vs 202 in the tower, so ~37-45 units are probably on this parcel (assessor 37, year 1900). Whether this is an older building rehabbed or an assessor split is unconfirmed.

name: Hampton Inn & Suites Providence Downtown (former Old Colony House bank building)
notes: 110-room hotel (matches assessor 110) in a 1920s bank tower, opened March 2009.

name: G Reserve (Union Trust Company Building)
notes: 12-story 1901 office tower converted to 61 apartments on floors 3-11 plus a rooftop penthouse; the Dorrance restaurant stays on the ground floor and offices on the 2nd. Completed 2019; owner sought a 15-year TSA (2018). Assessor 50 units. Office-to-residential, but CO 2019 is outside the ~5-year window.

name: Omni Providence Hotel (formerly Westin Providence)
notes: Opened 1994 as the Westin; Omni since Jan 2013. Room count is 511-564 depending on source (assessor 364 = original tower; the adjacent Residences tower added 200 rooms). In 2021 Brown leased 240 rooms as temporary student housing.

name: Grant Mill (299 Carpenter St)
notes: Mill converted to apartments in 2009 by Brady Sullivan, sold to a Heritage Properties affiliate in 2017. 85 units (53 1BR / 31 2BR / 1 3BR), rents ~$2,045-2,945; no affordability mentioned.

name: Regency Plaza (1 Regency Plaza)
notes: 1960s downtown high-rise rental complex marketed as 1 Regency Plaza; market rate (studios-3BR ~$1,805-6,810, applicants need 3x rent income), no subsidy found. This parcel (Regency Plaza I LLC) carries 192 assessor units of a multi-tower complex. Residents mention construction noise.

name: 257 Thayer
notes: Gilbane Development purpose-built private student housing for Brown/RISD: 95 suite-style apartments, 267 beds, furnished, per-person rents; replaced nine triple-deckers. First move-ins Jan 2015. Managed by Asset Campus Housing; not university-owned. Assessor 96 units.

name: 468 West Fountain St apartments
notes: New-construction rental building (listing gives year built 2022; assessor 2020; tax-stabilized) with 1-2BR units ~$1,700-2,695, quartz and in-unit W/D. Matched to 466 (W) Fountain parcel by adjacency and owner Unison West Fountain LLC; unit count from assessor. Likely inside the 5-year new-construction window.

name: 101 Hillside Ave apartments
notes: Elevator rental building in Hope area (studios-2BR, ~$1,450-2,600), managed by The Bilotti Group; NEREJ notes a $5M sale. Assessor class is Commercial Condo with 22 units, built 1985; units are rentals, not individually owned condos.

name: US Rubber Lofts (Eagle Square mill; owner LLC named Locomotive Works)
notes: Historic mill converted to loft apartments, managed by Brady Sullivan Properties; complex spans 11/12/22/25 Eagle St. Studio-4BR ~$1,735-3,405. Assessor 94 units on this parcel. Conversion year not found (probably 2000s mill-loft era, unverified). No affordability seen.

name: Hilton Garden Inn Providence (formerly Radisson Providence Harbor, then Wyndham Garden)
notes: India Point hotel, 136-137 rooms (assessor 136).

name: Aloft Providence Downtown
notes: ~175-room Marriott Aloft hotel (assessor 176), new building c.2021 (named 2022 Opening Aloft Hotel of the Year).

name: Nightingale Apartments (100 Mathewson St)
notes: New construction by Cornish Associates/Nordblom/Boston Andes on a full block (Fountain/Clemence/Washington/Mathewson): 143 studio-2BR market-rate units + 11,500 sf retail, $54M, opened Aug 2020. Rebuild RI tax credits ($6.1M) + sales-tax exemption; no affordable units mentioned. Developer entity was 78 Fountain JV Owner LLC. Opening is just outside the 5-year window.

name: Elmhurst Rehabilitation & Healthcare Center (50 Maude St; formerly Elmhurst Extended Care)
notes: 206-bed skilled nursing home (exactly matches assessor 206) in a commercial condo on the Roger Williams Medical Center campus; Tryko Partners bought it in 2016. Matched to this parcel by bed count and location, not by address; owner Valley Stream Property LLC is likely a Tryko real estate entity (unverified).

name: Emblem 125
notes: New-construction EQT Exeter tower (Bozzuto manages): 249 studio-3BR units + 19,398 sf retail. Leasing began June/July 2022, first residents Sept 2022. Studios from ~$2,100; no affordable units mentioned. Inside the ~5-year new-construction window.

name: Brown University residence hall + health and wellness center (450 Brook St)
notes: University-owned dorm for up to 162 upper-division undergraduates (suites with singles, shared kitchens) plus health/wellness services. First move-in May 2021, full opening Fall 2021. Assessor 219 units probably counts rooms/beds. Institutional dorm, exempt.

name: 34 Knight St apartments (Marcello Street Apartments)
notes: Brand-new elevator building off Atwells Ave in Federal Hill: PadMapper lists 29 units (matches assessor 29, owner 34 Knight Street LLC), 1-2BR ~$2,200-2,500. ForRent says built 2023 with 38 units/4 stories; assessor says 2022. Same building probably fronts Knight and Marcello St. Inside the 5-year new-construction window.

name: Rising Sun Mills
notes: Mill converted in 2004 by Armory Revival/Struever Bros to 135 lofts (31 studio / 69 1BR / 35 2BR) + 30,000 sf commercial; FPA Multifamily (FLT) bought it for $26.9M in Feb 2022. Market rate (~$1,780-3,699); no affordable units mentioned. Assessor 133, class Commercial Condo.

name: 49 Westfield Street Apartments (Rooms & Works; Stedman & Fuller / Bourn Rubber / Phillips-Baker Rubber Co. mill)
notes: Restored rubber-mill loft apartments: 64 units (Zumper; matches assessor 64), 1-2BR ~$1,875-2,900, managed by Rooms & Works Providence LLC. RI historic tax credit list (Apr 2024) shows the project as pending, est. completion Sept 2022, 0 units before and 28 after rehab (may be one phase only). Listings appear 2024-25, so residential opening is probably 2022-24, likely inside the 5-year window (not confirmed). Not the same as Westfield Lofts at 230 Dexter St.
